line: In business. N-vidia's shares briefly hit a record on Friday. They closed just below it, after a slump that wiped out over a trillion dollars.
In security. Apple will make it harder for apps to read everything on a Mac. It says A I agents raise the risk, but details are not out yet.
In energy. Oracle's new Wisconsin data center may run partly on nuclear power. State regulators must still approve the deal.
In robotics. The Pentagon may add up to fifty small robot boats on the Rio Grande. Ten already watch for illegal crossings, but nothing is decided.
In science. Meta says mathematicians used its chatbot to answer five open math questions. The claim is Meta's own, and other teams reached some of the same answers.
In health. Fewer high-risk patients died at eleven hospitals once A I alerts began. It only compared before and after, so the cause is not proven.
In society. Pope Leo wrote online that telling human art from machine art is becoming urgent. He said algorithms lack the spark of humanity.
And a lighter story. An Airbnb host reportedly billed a guest for a flooded toilet. The photo was A I made, and Google's chatbot found its hidden mark.
Also in the full report: a market for A I computing power may be coming. Some in the US want to ban chip machine sales to China.
And for the bigger picture: A I is now about who gets paid, and at what price. Companies spend less on it, but memory may cost more. Watch whether computing power trading begins.
